passages.P2: # Did Sean Connery Send a Letter to Apple Rejecting a Pitchman Offer?
passages.P3: ## The letter read, in part: "I can think of no quicker way to destroy my career than to appear in one of your crass adverts."
passages.P5: **RESTORED VERSION OF 'THE MAN WHO WOULD BE KING' (Photo by Colin McPherson/Sygma via Getty Images)**
passages.P7: A letter from actor Sean Connery rejects an offer for him to become a pitchman for Apple Computers.
passages.P8: An image of a purported 1998 letter from actor Sean Connery (famous for his portrayal of agent James Bond) to Apple CEO Steve Jobs, caustically rebuffing an offer to become a pitchman for Apple Computers, hit the Internet in June 2011.
passages.P9: Despite the letter's seeming verisimilitude, it was merely a bit of humor created as an accompaniment to an article published on the satirical site Scoopertino, which spoofs on all things Apple under the motto "All the News That's Fit to Fabricate".
passages.P10: Scoopertino's 19 June 2011 article entitled "EXPOSED: The iMac disaster that almost was" purported to offer a (fictional) episode from Apple's history, taken from the (equally fictional) book *iMaculate Conception: How Apple's iMac Was Born*, in which Apple CEO Steve Jobs supposedly sought to boost flagging holiday sales by soliciting actor Sean Connery to lend his name and visage to a 1998 Apple Christmas ad campaign:
passages.P11:
> As [former Apple marketing executive Frederica] Woods spins the tale, it was just weeks before iMac's first Christmas in 1998 when slowing holiday sales rang the alarm in the CEO's office.
>
> Steve Jobs, a lifelong fan of James Bond (he'd originally wanted to name the revolutionary computer "Double-O-Mac"), instructed his agency to begin work on a special celebrity Christmas ad featuring 007 himself, Sean Connery — even though Connery had yet to be signed.
>
> "The ad was of dubious quality, clearly not one of the agency's finer moments," says Woods.
passages.P12: The article noted that "Connery's final rejection was accompanied by a note revealing one mightily peeved film star," as revealed in the fabricated letter reproduced above.
passages.P13: Other spoofs from Scoopertino include "Madame Tussauds opens Apple iChamber of Horrors," "Bill Gates predicts 'Apple Rapture': all Macs to explode in 2012," and "VATICAN SHOCKER: Cardinals tap Siri as next pope."
passages.P15: Acierno, Louis J. "The History of Cardiology."    *Parthenon Publishing Group.* 1994. ISBN 1-85070-339-6 (pp. 469-476).
passages.P17: David Mikkelson founded the site now known as snopes.com back in 1994.

passages.P1: # Connery's Fictional Letter to Jobs Goes Viral
passages.P2: #### Published June 21, 2011 • Updated on June 22, 2011 at 7:50 am
passages.P3: Twitter is slowly graduating from prematurely killing off celebrities to brilliantly imitating them.
passages.P4: The latest bit of misinformation to go viral on Twitter involves Sean Connery writing a letter to Apple CEO Steve Jobs.
passages.P5: But like so much on Twitter, the letter is completely fabricated but that doesn't take away from the humor -- as long as you have a pretty decen Sean Connery voice in your head. Keep that handy for later.
passages.P6: The fake letter allegedly involves the former James Bond actor turning down the legendary founder of Apple's proposal for Connery to be a spokesperson for the company.
passages.P7: Dust out your best Sean Connery voice and read the fake letter below:
passages.P8:
> Mr Jobs:  
>   
> I will say this one more time. You do understand English, don't you? I do not sell my soul for Apple or any other company. I have interest in "changing the world" as you suggest. You have nothing that I need or want. You are a computer salesman -- I am f---ing JAMES BOND!  
>   
> I can think of no quicker way to destroy my career than to appear in one of your crass adverts. Please do not contact me again.  
>   
> Best,  
>   
> Sean Connery
passages.P9: The letter, complete on 007 letterhead, has been making the rounds on Twitter. But it's obviously not real. It comes from the fake Mac rumor site Scoopertino, which claims the letter comes from a book called iMaculate Conception: How Apple’s iMac Was Born.
passages.P10: The letter doesn't mean anything but it's worth a laugh and it sure beats tweeting the fake death of either Connery or Jobs.
